text:
Lesson three, the tipping widget itself. The widget is the part of the attention page where money actually moves, and the mechanic that matters most is tip tiers. A tip tier is a named preset amount with its own identity, like a three dollar espresso or a ten dollar latte.

Here is the decision framework. Fixed tiers exist because choosing an amount is work, and work kills conversion. A supporter who has to invent a number hesitates. A supporter who taps espresso does not. So tiers convert better than a blank custom field, and this is not ideology, it is measured across every tipping platform that publishes numbers.

The edge case: custom amounts still matter, but only above the top tier. If you cap the maximum or hide the custom field, you lose whales, and whales are a disproportionate share of revenue. So the rule is tiers for the median supporter, open field for the generous ones.

A warning on implementation. Tip with message looks like a small feature but it is the seed of the supporter loop we cover next lesson. A tip with a note is the beginning of a relationship. A tip without one is a transaction. Build the message field first, and never charge extra for it, because the moment it costs money nobody writes one.
